rounds.text: Quality Power Electrical Equipments Ltd is backed by exceptional operational profitability, demonstrated by a ROCE of 38.32% against a sector benchmark of 12.63% [E10] and a median return on equity of 25% over three years [E20]. Growth metrics are explosive, featuring a compounded sales growth of 122% over the trailing twelve months [E15] and compounded profit growth of 90% over the same period [E17], supported by an operating margin expansion of 6 percentage points to 19% [E22]. Market momentum completely validates these fundamentals, with the stock holding a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E44], a Sharpe ratio of 1.69 [E48], and trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E43]. Furthermore, the business is operating in a clear macro sweet spot with Capital Goods identified in a tailwind with a score of +1.04 [E66], while maintaining a conservative financial profile with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.07x [E30]. Conceded: the stock trades at a rich valuation including a P/E of 82.8 [E1], a price-to-book of 20.33x [E2], and a negative margin of safety under a DCF model [E39].

Quality Power Electrical Equipments Ltd is exhibiting explosive, top-tier growth that comfortably outpaces the broader sector [E68]. Compounded sales growth over 3 years hits 55%, accelerating to an extraordinary 122% over the trailing twelve months, while profit growth compounds at 81% and 90% respectively [E14, E15, E16, E17]. This fundamental outperformance is backed by elite capital efficiency, highlighted by a stellar ROCE of 38.32% against a sector benchmark of just 12.63%, alongside a median return on equity of 25% over the last three years [E10, E20]. Operating margins have also expanded by 6 percentage points to reach 19% in the TTM period [E22], while the business maintains an ultra-conservative balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.07x and strong short-term liquidity [E30, E31]. Furthermore, the company benefits from a powerful macro sector tailwind score of +1.04 in Capital Goods [E64, E66], drives positive institutional money flow with a holding change increase of 1.57 percentage points [E37], and boasts a maximum relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 alongside a healthy Sharpe ratio of 1.69 [E44, E48]. Conceded: [E38], [E63].

The bull highlights stellar growth and capital efficiency, but fundamental operating cash realities severely undermine these high-flying metrics [E14, E15, E10]. Conceded: [E10, E14, E15, E16, E17, E20]. Cash conversion sits at a worrisome 0.43x for Mar 2026, meaning reported profits are running far ahead of actual cash collected, pointing straight toward receivables and accruals issues [E26]. That profit disconnect translates directly into negative free cash flow of Rs -31 Cr for Mar 2026, alongside operating cash flow lagging at just 64% of operating profit [E28, E29]. Furthermore, earnings quality is explicitly flagged by the presence of Rs 66.1 Cr in other income inflating the bottom line [E55]. Borrowings have also spiked to Rs 40 Cr from Rs 9 Cr a year earlier, and capital work-in-progress has surged by 3550% to Rs 73 Cr, representing an uncompleted capex build-up phase that introduces heavy execution and financing risk [E32, E33]. Finally, the screen explicitly warns that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E61].

Conceded: [E26, E28, E29, E32, E33, E55]. While cash conversion and free cash flow experienced near-term pressure in March 2026 alongside a spike in borrowings and capital work-in-progress, this massive 3550.0% capex build-up to Rs 73 Cr represents active growth spend underway rather than structural failure [E28, E32, E33]. The company maintains robust financial positioning with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.07x and solid short-term liquidity through a current ratio of 2.90x [E30, E31]. Furthermore, institutional money flow reads positive with a holding increase of 1.57 percentage points, showing that professional capital is backing the expansion phase [E37]. The business operates within a high-conviction Capital Goods sector tailwind scoring +1.04, supported by stellar operational metrics including a 38.32% ROCE that vastly outperforms the sector benchmark of 12.63% [E10, E66]. Finally, the rules-based screen scores the company an 83 out of 100 with a BUY rating, driven by powerful sales growth of 32% year-over-year [E56, E57].

Conceded: [E30, E31, E37, E56, E57]. While debt-to-equity sits at a conservative 0.07x and the rules-based screen scores an 83 out of 100 with a BUY rating backed by positive institutional money flow, these structural strengths do not negate the severe cash flow disconnection [E30, E31, E37, E56, E57]. The massive 3550.0% surge in capital work-in-progress to Rs 73 Cr and the rise in borrowings from Rs 9 Cr to Rs 40 Cr are precisely why free cash flow plunged to Rs -31 Cr and cash conversion dropped to a concerning 0.43x, demonstrating that growth is currently being fueled by cash burn rather than internal generation [E26, E28, E32, E33]. Furthermore, relying on an 38.32% ROCE ignores the fact that reported earnings are significantly inflated by Rs 66.1 Cr in other income, casting doubt on core operating quality [E10, E55]. Finally, pointing to a sector tailwind score of +1.04 does nothing to justify a staggering P/E ratio of 82.8x and a price-to-book of 20.33x that vastly outpace sector benchmarks [E1, E2, E6, E7, E66].
